Who We Are

The Mind Behind Talented Scholar Digitals

Talented Scholar Digitals was founded by Fawaz, an eCommerce specialist and digital solutions strategist. What started as a Shopify development practice has grown into a complete eCommerce and digital solutions agency, helping brands build, optimize, market, and scale their entire online presence.

In 2024, Fawaz graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from the prestigious University of Ilorin, one of Nigeria's foremost academic institutions. That technical foundation, combined with years of hands-on experience across multiple agencies, shapes how every project is planned and delivered today.

Along the way, Fawaz has worked across different agency environments and currently collaborates with Zenthrop Agency on select client engagements, bringing an extra layer of creative and strategic firepower to larger projects. This network of collaboration means clients get the personal attention of a dedicated specialist backed by the capacity of a wider team.

Collaboration note: Several stores in this portfolio were delivered in partnership with established Shopify Partner agencies and with Zenthrop Agency as part of ongoing professional growth. Great work is often built together.

Vision

To be the go-to digital partner for businesses that want to build, market, and scale a real online presence, not just a website.

Mission

To combine eCommerce development, marketing, creative design, and content into one dependable growth engine for every client.

Values

Honest communication, strategic thinking, and craftsmanship in every deliverable, from a single product page to a full brand launch.

eCommerce Build

RunTribe

ChallengeA running-gear brand needed a store built from scratch that could also handle event registrations for community runs.
SolutionA custom Shopify build with a bespoke event-registration flow layered on top of the standard product catalog.
ProcessDiscovery, architecture planning, custom section development, and full device testing before launch.

Theme & Brand

Tsonga

ChallengeA premium footwear brand expanding into Australia needed a theme that matched a higher-end market without losing brand identity.
SolutionA full custom theme with tailored collection pages and a localised shopping experience for the new market.
ProcessBrand audit, wireframing, custom theme development, and staged review rounds with the client.

Speed Optimization

Multiple Client Stores

ChallengeSeveral existing stores were losing visitors to slow load times caused by oversized images and conflicting apps.
SolutionA full performance audit, image compression, script cleanup, and Core Web Vitals improvements.
ProcessBaseline audit, bottleneck diagnosis, optimization pass, and a before-and-after report for each store.
Tools UsedShopify theme code, image compression tooling, Core Web Vitals reporting.
Result: load times cut significantly across every optimized store, with measurable gains in conversion behavior.

Common Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Straight answers to the questions clients ask most before starting a project.

Which eCommerce platforms do you work with?
Shopify is the core specialty, but the agency also builds and supports WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and Wix eCommerce stores, along with custom builds where needed.
Do you only build stores, or do you handle marketing too?
Both. Alongside store builds, the agency offers SEO, Google Ads, social and email marketing, and content strategy, so a store isn't left without traffic after launch.
How long does a typical Shopify build take?
Most builds take between 2 and 6 weeks depending on scope, from a simple store setup to a fully custom theme with advanced app integrations.
Can you migrate my existing store to Shopify?
Yes. Migrations from WooCommerce, Wix, or BigCommerce are handled with full data preservation and redirect mapping to protect existing SEO rankings.
Do you offer eBook writing and publishing services?
Yes. This covers writing or ghostwriting, editing, formatting, cover design, and publishing support on Amazon KDP and other marketplaces.
How do I get started?
Fill in the enquiry form below or book a free consultation call. A short discovery conversation is the first step on every project.

Services, In Detail

Store Setup and Launch

Full Shopify setup from scratch, from domain to first sale.

If you're starting fresh, this is where it begins. I set up your entire Shopify store from the ground up: domain connection, theme installation, product catalog, collections, payment gateways, shipping zones, and every legal and policy page a store needs before it can accept a single order. You bring the products and the vision. I handle the technical build so you launch with confidence, not guesswork.

What's Included

  • Domain connection and store settings configuration
  • Theme installation and initial setup
  • Product upload, variants, and collection structuring
  • Payment gateway setup (Paystack, Stripe, PayPal, and more)
  • Shipping zones and tax configuration
  • Policy pages, legal pages, and pre-launch checklist

My Process

  1. Discovery call to understand your brand and goals
  2. Store architecture and sitemap planning
  3. Build and configure every core setting
  4. Upload products and organize collections
  5. Full testing across devices and checkout flow
  6. Launch day support and post-launch check-in
Recent stores launched from scratch include RunTribe, a running gear and community brand with event registration built in, and SweetBakes Co., an artisan bakery brand with a custom cake-order and booking system.
Enquire About This Service

Theme Design and Customization

Custom, pixel-perfect themes built around your brand, not a template.

Templates are a starting point, not a finished product. Every store I design gets a custom look built around your brand's colors, typography, and personality, with hand-built sections and layouts that no other store on the internet has. This is where your store stops looking like everyone else's Shopify theme and starts looking like your brand.

What's Included

  • Full brand audit and visual direction
  • Custom homepage and landing page sections
  • Typography and color system built into the theme
  • Custom Liquid sections for unique layouts
  • Fully responsive design across all screen sizes
  • Interactive elements: hover states, animations, and micro-interactions

My Process

  1. Brand and competitor audit
  2. Wireframing key pages and user flows
  3. Visual design and style guide creation
  4. Theme development and section building
  5. Client review and revision rounds
  6. Final handover with documentation
Tsonga, a premium footwear brand, received a full custom theme with tailored collection pages and a localised experience for their Australian market expansion.

⚡

Store Speed Optimization

Faster load times, better Core Web Vitals, higher conversions.

A slow store loses sales before a visitor even sees your products. I run a full speed audit on your store, identify exactly what is slowing it down (usually oversized images, bloated apps, or unoptimized code), and fix it. The result is a store that loads fast on every device and ranks better with search engines that reward speed.

What's Included

  • Full speed and performance audit
  • Image compression and lazy-loading setup
  • Theme code cleanup and script optimization
  • Core Web Vitals improvements (LCP, CLS, INP)
  • Third-party app script audit and cleanup
  • Before-and-after performance report

My Process

  1. Run a baseline speed audit
  2. Diagnose the biggest bottlenecks
  3. Optimize images, code, and app scripts
  4. Re-test across mobile and desktop
  5. Deliver a clear before-and-after report
Multiple client stores have seen load times cut by more than half after an optimization pass, directly improving their conversion rates.
Enquire About This Service
📱

Responsive Mobile Optimization

Built mobile-first, because that's where over 70% of shoppers are.

Most shoppers today are browsing and buying from their phones, not a desktop. I build and audit stores with mobile as the priority, not an afterthought: touch-friendly navigation, thumb-reachable buttons, a checkout that doesn't fight the user, and layouts that were actually designed for a small screen rather than just shrunk down to fit one.

What's Included

  • Mobile-first layout and navigation design
  • Touch-friendly buttons and menus
  • Mobile checkout flow optimization
  • Cross-device and cross-browser testing
  • Image and font scaling for smaller screens

My Process

  1. Audit current mobile experience
  2. Redesign problem areas for touch and thumb reach
  3. Rebuild layouts mobile-first, then scale up
  4. Test across real devices, not just browser previews
  5. Confirm checkout completion flow is frictionless
Every store I build is tested on real iOS and Android devices before launch, not just resized in a browser window.

Shopify Apps Installation and Configuration

Reviews, email marketing, loyalty, and subscriptions, working together, not against each other.

The Shopify App Store has a solution for almost everything, but installing five apps that quietly conflict with each other is how stores end up slow and buggy. I choose the right apps for your specific goals, configure them properly, and make sure they work together cleanly, whether that's product reviews, email marketing automation, loyalty programs, or subscriptions.

What's Included

  • App selection based on your actual business needs
  • Reviews and social proof app setup (Loox, Judge.me, and similar)
  • Email marketing integration (Klaviyo and others)
  • Loyalty and subscription app configuration
  • Conflict testing between installed apps
  • Ongoing app maintenance available

My Process

  1. Review your goals and current app stack
  2. Recommend and install the right tools
  3. Configure each app to match your workflow
  4. Test for conflicts and performance impact
  5. Document what was installed and why
Several stores now run integrated review, email, and loyalty systems that were previously fighting each other before a clean reconfiguration.
Enquire About This Service
🚀

Shopify Migration

Moving to Shopify from WooCommerce, Wix, or BigCommerce, with zero data loss.

Switching platforms is intimidating because of everything you could lose: products, customer data, order history, and your search rankings. I handle full migrations to Shopify with a careful, tested process that preserves your data and puts proper redirects in place so you don't lose the SEO equity you've already built.

What's Included

  • Full product, customer, and order data migration
  • URL redirect mapping to protect SEO rankings
  • Theme rebuild on Shopify matching or improving your current design
  • Payment and shipping reconfiguration
  • Full testing before DNS cutover
  • Post-migration monitoring

My Process

  1. Audit your existing store and export all data
  2. Plan the migration and redirect map
  3. Rebuild the store on Shopify
  4. Import and verify all data
  5. Test thoroughly, then switch DNS
  6. Monitor closely in the days after launch
Store migrations completed to date have moved with zero lost orders and no meaningful drop in search rankings post-launch.

Why Talented Scholar Digitals

Why Choose Us, In Detail

A closer look at what actually backs up every claim on the homepage.

One Team, Every DisciplineTechnical FoundationAgency-Level CollaborationStrategy Before PixelsTransparent CommunicationSupport After Launch

One Team, Every Discipline

eCommerce development, marketing, creative, and eBook publishing under one point of contact.

Most stores don't fail because of one bad decision, they fail because five different freelancers each did their one piece without talking to each other: a developer who never spoke to the marketer, a designer who never saw the SEO plan. Working with a single point of contact means the store build, the marketing strategy, the brand visuals, and any eBook or content assets are all planned together from day one, so they reinforce each other instead of working against each other.

What this looks like

  • One person accountable for the whole project outcome
  • Design decisions made with SEO and conversion in mind from the start
  • Marketing assets that match the store's actual brand system
  • No handoff delays between disconnected vendors

Why it matters

  • Fewer inconsistencies between what a store looks like and how it's marketed
  • Faster turnaround since nothing waits on a second vendor's schedule
  • One clear person to reach when something needs to change

Technical Foundation

A Computer Science background means every build is engineered properly, not just styled to look good.

A lot of Shopify work is done by people who are strong designers but treat the underlying code as a black box. A technical background changes what's possible: custom Liquid sections instead of settling for what a theme allows, real performance diagnostics instead of guesswork, and app integrations that don't quietly break each other. It's the difference between a store that looks right on launch day and one that stays fast, stable, and easy to extend a year later.

What this looks like

  • Custom Liquid, JavaScript, and API work when templates fall short
  • Real diagnosis of speed and Core Web Vitals issues, not surface fixes
  • Clean, documented code that's easy to hand off or extend later

Why it matters

  • Fewer app conflicts and fewer mystery bugs after launch
  • A store that can grow past what out-of-the-box themes support
  • Lower long-term maintenance cost

Agency-Level Collaboration

Partnerships with Zenthrop Agency and other Shopify Partners bring extra capacity to larger projects.

Some projects are bigger than one person, whether that's a tight deadline, a multi-region rollout, or a build that needs several specialists working in parallel. Rather than turning that work away or rushing it, established partner relationships mean extra hands can be brought in when a project genuinely calls for it, without losing the single point of contact and accountability that comes with working directly with Talented Scholar Digitals.

What this looks like

  • Additional developer and design capacity for larger builds
  • Faster delivery on tight-deadline projects
  • Still one accountable point of contact throughout

Why it matters

  • Larger or more complex projects don't have to be turned down
  • Quality doesn't slip just because a timeline is tight

Strategy Before Pixels

Every project starts with your business goals, not a template, so the work is built to convert.

A store that looks beautiful but doesn't sell has solved the wrong problem. Before any design work starts, the project begins with the actual business questions: who the customer is, what's stopping them from buying today, and what the store needs to do in the first 90 days. That strategy shapes every decision that follows, from navigation structure to the checkout flow, instead of design happening first and strategy getting bolted on afterward.

What this looks like

  • A discovery conversation before any design or build work begins
  • Navigation and page structure built around how customers actually shop
  • Design choices tied back to a specific conversion goal

Why it matters

  • A store built to sell, not just to look good in a portfolio
  • Less rework later because the goals were clear from the start

Transparent Communication

Clear timelines, honest scoping, and no disappearing after the invoice is paid.

One of the most common complaints about freelance work isn't quality, it's silence: a vendor who goes quiet after being paid, or who agrees to anything during scoping and then delivers something different. Every project starts with a clear, written scope and timeline, and updates happen proactively instead of only when asked. If something needs to change mid-project, that gets flagged immediately rather than discovered at delivery.

What this looks like

  • A written scope and timeline agreed before work begins
  • Proactive progress updates, not just replies when asked
  • Honest pushback if a request will hurt the store's performance

Why it matters

  • No surprises at delivery
  • Trust that builds into repeat projects, not one-off jobs

Support After Launch

Stores and campaigns are monitored after go-live, not abandoned the day they ship.

Launch day is the start of a store's life, not the end of the project. Traffic patterns, app updates, and seasonal changes all affect a live store in ways that are hard to predict in advance. Post-launch monitoring catches issues, like a broken checkout step or a slow-loading page, before they cost real sales, and gives clients a place to turn when something needs adjusting after go-live.

What this looks like

  • Post-launch checks on speed, checkout, and key store functions
  • A clear channel for reporting and resolving issues after go-live
  • Guidance on updates as the store's needs change over time

Why it matters

  • Small issues get caught before they affect sales
  • A long-term relationship instead of a one-time transaction

Store Optimization

5 Signs Your Store Is Losing Sales (and How to Fix Them)

Most store owners assume a slow month means they need more traffic. Sometimes that's true, but more often the visitors are already showing up and quietly leaving without buying. Here are five of the most common leaks, and the fix for each.

The five leaks

  • A checkout with too many steps. Every extra field or page is a chance for someone to abandon. A one-page or accordion-style checkout with guest checkout enabled removes friction fast.
  • Product pages that describe but don't sell. A list of specs answers "what is this" but not "why should I buy it." Pair specs with a short outcome-focused paragraph.
  • No urgency or social proof. Stock counters, recent-sale notifications, and genuine reviews all reduce hesitation at the exact moment someone is deciding.
  • Slow load times on mobile. Most traffic is mobile now, and a store that takes more than three seconds to load loses a meaningful share of visitors before the page even finishes rendering.
  • No abandoned cart recovery. A large share of carts are never completed. A simple two or three-email recovery flow reclaims a portion of that revenue automatically.

Where to start

  • Pull up your store's analytics and look for the exact step where visitors drop off
  • Fix the single biggest leak first rather than trying to fix everything at once
  • Re-measure after each change so you know what actually moved the needle

Platform Strategy

Shopify vs WooCommerce vs Wix: Choosing the Right Platform

There's no single "best" eCommerce platform, only the right one for your product, budget, and growth plans. Here's a straightforward way to think about the decision instead of just picking whatever's trending.

When each one fits

  • Shopify suits brands that want a hosted, low-maintenance store with a huge app ecosystem and room to scale into high order volumes.
  • WooCommerce suits businesses already invested in WordPress, or that need deep, low-level customization and don't mind managing hosting themselves.
  • Wix suits very small catalogs and service-based sellers who want the absolute simplest setup and aren't planning rapid growth.

Questions worth answering first

  • How many products, and how fast do you expect that to grow?
  • Do you need specific integrations like ERP, wholesale pricing, or subscriptions?
  • Who will maintain the store day-to-day once it's live?

Copywriting

How to Write Product Descriptions That Actually Convert

Most product pages describe features and hope for the best. A description that actually sells follows a simple structure: lead with the outcome, back it up with specifics, then remove the remaining doubt.

A simple structure

  • Open with the outcome. What does owning this actually change for the customer? Lead with that, not the material or dimensions.
  • Follow with specifics. Size, materials, and features matter, but only after the reader already cares about the outcome.
  • Close the remaining doubt. Shipping time, return policy, or a one-line guarantee removes the last hesitation before checkout.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Writing the same generic copy for every variant of a product
  • Burying the most persuasive detail at the bottom of a long paragraph
  • Skipping real customer language, the exact words buyers use in reviews and messages

Performance

The Real Cost of a Slow Store

A slow store doesn't announce itself, visitors just quietly leave. Every additional second of load time chips away at conversion rate, and on mobile connections that effect is even sharper. The good news is that speed problems are usually fixable without a full rebuild.

What usually slows a store down

  • Oversized, uncompressed product images
  • Too many apps loading scripts on every single page
  • Bloated or poorly coded theme sections
  • Render-blocking third-party scripts like chat widgets and pop-ups

Where to start

  • Run a baseline speed test and note your Core Web Vitals scores
  • Compress and lazy-load images before touching anything else
  • Audit installed apps and remove anything not actively earning its keep

eBook Publishing

From Manuscript to Marketplace: A Simple Guide to Amazon KDP

Self-publishing looks intimidating from the outside, mostly because of formatting and metadata that nobody explains clearly. Broken into steps, it's far more manageable than most first-time authors expect.

The core steps

  • Finish and edit the manuscript before worrying about any formatting or cover work.
  • Format for both eBook and print if you plan to offer a paperback, since the layout requirements differ.
  • Design a cover built for thumbnail size, since most readers will first see it as a tiny image in search results.
  • Write metadata with intent: title, subtitle, categories, and keywords all affect discoverability on Amazon.
  • Set pricing and enroll appropriately depending on whether KDP Select fits your distribution plans.

Common first-time mistakes

  • Publishing with an unformatted manuscript, causing awkward breaks on Kindle
  • Choosing overly broad categories that bury the book in competition
  • Skipping a proper launch plan, so the book never gets an early sales push

Digital Marketing

The Email Flows Every eCommerce Store Needs

Most stores only send email when there's a sale to announce. Automated flows work in the background every day, and they usually convert far better than one-off campaigns because they're triggered by something the customer just did.

Three flows to start with

  • Welcome flow. Sent to new subscribers, introducing the brand and often including a first-purchase incentive.
  • Abandoned cart flow. A short two or three-email sequence reminding a visitor about the items left behind.
  • Post-purchase flow. Order updates, a request for a review, and a well-timed nudge toward a second purchase.

Why flows outperform one-off campaigns

  • They're triggered by real customer behavior, not a calendar date
  • They keep working without needing to be manually sent each time
  • They tend to have higher open and click rates than broadcast campaigns
